items.title: The invariants of the inertia group form the integral closure of a Galois subextension, and the corresponding local extension is etale
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K, a finite Galois extension L/K, a maximal ideal m of the integral closure B of A in L, and the inertia group I of m, and asserts that B^I is the integral closure of A in L^I and that A -> (B^I)_{B^I cap m} is etale (source lines 33474-33482). The proof is a genuine index computation. It writes B' = B^I and m' = B' cap m, uses that m is the unique prime of B over m', and notes that since I acts trivially on kappa(m) the extension kappa(m)/kappa(m') is purely inseparable, so D/I acts faithfully on kappa(m'); then Galois theory gives [kappa(m') : kappa] >= |D/I| (proof lines 33485-33500). The substantive part is a numerical comparison of the two degree formulae: using that Norm_{L/K}(pi) = pi^{[L:K]} one gets |G| = [L:K] = |G/D| [kappa(m):kappa] ord_{B_m}(pi), and applying the same reasoning to L/L^I of degree |I| gives |I| ord_{B'_{m'}}(pi) = [kappa(m):kappa(m')] ord_{B_m}(pi) (proof lines 33502-33520 and following). Combining these with the Galois-theoretic bound on [kappa(m'):kappa] forces the ramification index of the local extension to be 1 and the residue extension to be separable, which is exactly etaleness. The non-routine content is the interplay of the ramification-index multiplicativity, the norm formula for the uniformizer and the bound coming from faithfulness of the action of D/I on the residue field.
